title: The symmetric-product morphism is a morphism over the base
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme and $n\ge1$. Write $\mathbf P^1_S=\mathbf P(\{0,1\};S)$ and $\mathbf P^n_S=\mathbf P(\{0,\dots,n\};S)$ [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change], with structure morphisms $q_1:\mathbf P^1_S\to S$ and $q_n:\mathbf P^n_S\to S$, and let $(\mathbf P^1_S)^n=\mathbf P^1_S\times_S\cdots\times_S\mathbf P^1_S$ be the $n$-fold fibre product over $S$ [def-pc-fibre-product], with its projection $p_n:(\mathbf P^1_S)^n\to S$. Then the symmetric-product morphism $\sigma_n:(\mathbf P^1_S)^n\to\mathbf P^n_S$ of [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-product-properties], given by $((x_1:y_1),\dots,(x_n:y_n))\mapsto[F_0:\cdots:F_n]$ with $\prod_i(x_it+y_i)=\sum_jF_jt^j$, is a morphism over $S$: $q_n\circ\sigma_n=p_n$.

source.place: Lemma 0A4F (label lemma-reduce-to-P1), proof, last paragraph ("For every $n \geq 1$ there is a finite surjective morphism ... Applying Lemmas 0A4C, 0A4E, 0A4D one more time"): the $F_j$ are polynomials with integer coefficients, so the morphism is defined over $\mathbf Z$ and base changed to $S$; the source uses $q_n\circ\sigma_n=p_n$ implicitly when it applies Lemma 0A4C
